title: Axiom hubfold switchboard: slimline workspace lenses & contextual rail proposal
creator: Asha Patel
description: Proposal and prototype for a compact, permission-aware navigation rail ("slimline contextual rail") plus a lightweight workspace lens switcher ("hubfold") that surfaces per-workspace dashboards, rollouts, and cost views with minimal top-level chrome. This ticket captures the IA diagram, interaction spec, accessibility notes, and handoff assets for engineering and product review.
problem_statement: The current console navigation mixes global routes, workspace context, and feature surfaces in ways that create deep click paths for common tasks: checking per-model cost, viewing a rollout status, or switching quickly between dev/staging/workspace sandboxes. Users report friction in reaching cost breakdowns and rollouts during incidents or capacity checks. This increases time-to-incident-diagnosis and discourages exploratory monitoring.
goals: 1) Reduce time-to-action for three common flows: workspace switch, open per-route cost breakdown, and inspect rollout status. 2) Surface high-value metrics (cost TPU/GPU, p95 latency, active sessions) within two taps. 3) Maintain consistent keyboard nav and screen-reader semantics. 4) Keep top-level chrome compact to prioritize content space for dashboards.
proposed_solution_summary: Introduce a slimline contextual rail anchored to the left of the console: collapsed by default on narrow screens, expanded on hover/focus. The rail contains a role-aware workspace lens at the top that shows the active workspace avatar and a quick-switcher menu (recent, pinned, favorite). Below the lens are compact route chips (Dashboards, Rollouts, Models, Cost, Alerts). Selecting a chip opens a slide-over with the relevant route content; for primary routes (Dashboards, Cost, Rollouts) we allow pinning to the main canvas. The rail also implements progressive disclosure: rarely-used items are nested under a "More" chevron to reduce visual noise.
acceptance_criteria: Keyboard focus can traverse the rail, open the quick-switcher, and activate route chips (tab/shift-tab and enter/space).
Screen reader announces workspace lens context and the selected route chip.
Two-tap path to open Cost breakdown from any console route (rail chip -> cost slide-over) verified in usability test with 5 users.
Pinned dashboard instances persist per-user and per-workspace and are restored on reload.
Collapsed rail reduces to 48px width and expands on hover/focus without content shift beyond 16px to avoid layout jumps.
decisions: Use a slide-over for quick route previews rather than full navigation to preserve context and speed back-and-forth exploration.
Workspace quick-switcher will surface 5 recent + 3 pinned workspaces; we will add a full search modal in a follow-up ticket to avoid scope creep.
Cost chip shows a micro-summary (24h spend + delta) inline; clicking opens the full cost view with tokenized breakdowns.
Role-aware items: admin-only routes are visually flagged and require confirmation to pin to the main canvas.
tradeoffs: Slide-overs are fast for quick checks but can obscure complex dashboards; we mitigate by allowing pin-to-canvas for power users. Compact rail reduces discoverability of low-frequency tools; we offset by retaining a persistent "More" chevron and keyboard shortcuts. Implementing per-user pinned canvas state increases storage complexity for engineering (requires a small user preferences API).
review_feedback: PM (Lena Gómez): 'Love the micro-summary on cost — make sure the delta uses color blind-safe palettes and an icon label.'

Eng (Diego Morales): 'Slide-over approach looks good; need precise SLOs for opening times and a fallback for slow RPCs (skeletons + optimistic state). API contract to return quick-summary in <150ms is requested.'
Design (Ravi Srinivasan): 'Consider a subtle badge for environments with active incidents; also suggest a condensed mode for >3 workspaces.'
open_questions: Should pinned canvas state sync across devices or stay local to the browser?
What is the canonical endpoint for the 24h cost micro-summary and will it be cached?
How should we handle very long workspace names in the lens UI to avoid overflow?
accessibility_notes: All action targets must be >=44px on touch and have 1.5:1 focus contrast. Labelling: workspace lens must expose aria-current and route chips require aria-pressed toggles for pin state. Keyboard shortcuts: Cmd/Ctrl+K opens the quick-switcher; numbers 1-5 switch pinned dashboards.
perf_considerations: Render the rail as a composited layer to avoid reflows on expand; fetch micro-summary data via a separate low-priority endpoint with caching headers (60s). Use skeleton loaders for slide-over content and graceful failure states for backend timeouts.
handoff_instructions: 1) Reference Figma frames 12-18 for expanded/collapsed states and motion specs. 2) Provide CSS variables for widths and animation durations. 3) Engineering to add endpoints: /api/workspaces/quick-list and /api/workspaces/{id}/micro-cost. 4) Include unit tests for keyboard navigation and snapshot tests for rail states.
next_steps: 1) Address Eng feedback on API latency; add ENG spike ticket for micro-summary caching. 2) Usability test (5 users) for two-tap cost flow next week. 3) Finalize color tokens for delta palettes and add to design tokens. 4) Schedule handoff sync with frontend and platform on 2025-02-24.
